details: Goldman Sachs economists believe a Federal Reserve interest rate increase in September is "very unlikely," citing two months of weaker jobs and inflation data, including a decline in US retail sales in July. The firm noted that only a few Federal Open Market Committee members seemed inclined towards rate hikes as of the June meeting. This outlook suggests a potential easing of monetary tightening pressures, which could impact risk assets like cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin has historically reacted to Fed decisions, with recent rate holds often followed by declines.
title: Goldman Sachs Sees Unlikely Fed Rate Hike in September

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is reportedly preparing a regulatory framework to allow for 24/7 continuous trading of tokenized U.S. stocks on blockchain networks. This initiative involves creating an "innovation exemption" for selected platforms to test tokenized securities under defined conditions. SEC Chair Paul Atkins is expected to meet with key financial industry players to discuss the framework. This move could integrate traditional finance and digital asset technology, potentially boosting liquidity and adoption for blockchain-based securities.
title: SEC Plans Framework for 24/7 Tokenized Stock Trading
